status: NOT FROZEN, NOT RUN. Freeze with a fresh freeze.json and vault log before any outcome of the new release is read.
question: Once verification is paid for, does a feedback model that separates measurement-specific (plate/orientation) effects from shared drug-in-line effects find more verified discoveries per measurement than static retrieval with verify-hits allocation?
why_this: Registered result: in-context drug-in-line feedback gave NO_MEANINGFUL_GAIN in validated discoveries (G -1.1% [-4.0, +1.4]); its changed decisions raise screen calls and lower validation calls.

Post hoc: drug-in-line effects transfer across independent measurements with r 0.16-0.36 and negative out-of-orientation R2, so a model must learn from replicated measurements to learn anything reproducible.
Exploratory: verify-hits allocation gives +16% [12, 21] verified discoveries over paired measurement at equal measurements; feedback adds nothing to it as built.

candidates: Nair et al. 2023 Nat Commun NSCLC anchored screen (21 anchors x 242 library x 81 lines; second-facility validation on 15 lines)
any GDSC anchored release not used here
requirements: both drug orientations (or two independent measurements) for a complete, design-defined menu
plate identifiers to assert screen/validation plate disjointness
the authors' synergy rule and QC
at least about 60 lines with menus of at least about 100 pairs
design columns only read before freeze
data_gate.refusal: DATA_NOT_QUALIFIED if any requirement fails; record the census and stop

part_A_arms.static_verify_hits: history_mean ranking; each round verifies earlier unverified screen hits first (registered best policy in the exploratory follow-up)
part_A_arms.feedback_verify_hits: frozen in-context posterior on screen measurements only (the registered null, as a reference)
part_A_arms.replicate_aware_feedback_verify_hits: in-context model with two effect blocks: shared drug-in-line effects (fed by both screen and verification measurements) and orientation-specific drug effects (fed by one orientation only); ranking uses the shared block only; variances fitted on history lines only

budget: M = ceil(0.20 x menu) measurements per line in 4 rounds
primary_endpoint: verified discoveries per line (pairs measured in both orientations and synergistic in both), replicate_aware_feedback_verify_hits minus static_verify_hits
meaningful_gain: G >= 0.10 (a 4x longer campaign must buy at least 10% more verified discoveries); categories and stop guard as in protocol/protocol.json
inference: stratified line bootstrap 10,000 (seed 20261003) and two-way lines x pairs sensitivity

part_B_certificate_decision_aid.question: Does a valid pooled yield bound change the terminal decision (buy the shortlist remainder vs move that budget) better than the model's claim or a plug-in audit rate, at matched dose points?
rules: valid pooled (or Bonferroni) lower bound >= tau
plug-in audit hit rate x remainder >= tau
part_B_certificate_decision_aid.tau: set from the cost ratio before evaluation; no tuning
endpoints: rate of remainders bought with fewer than tau hits (<= delta under the valid rule)
prerequisites: per-item ids and costs in receipts

stopping: one opening per release; any rerun is a logged second opening; no interim looks
